evals.prompt: Add tests for our new `applyDiscount(order, coupon)` function and the POST /orders/:id/discount endpoint in our Express + Prisma + Postgres app. We use Vitest.
evals.expected_output: Uses Vitest and existing test conventions; unit tests for applyDiscount with hand-derived literal expectations and edge cases (expired coupon, zero/negative totals, rounding); integration tests for the endpoint against a real Postgres (container or test DB) including unauthorized and cross-tenant cases; no mocking of Prisma; proves tests fail by breaking the code; reports in the after-writing format.
expectations: Uses Vitest rather than introducing another test framework
Unit tests use literal expected values rather than recomputing with the function's own logic
Endpoint tests run against a real database engine rather than a mocked Prisma client
Includes at least one authorization or error-path test for the endpoint
States how the tests were shown to fail (breaking the code or reproducing a bug)
Report lists removed/skipped/weakened tests (or 'none') and what was not checked

evals.prompt: Our Playwright test 'user can export report' fails maybe 1 in 10 runs in CI. It has `await page.waitForTimeout(3000)` before checking the download, and the report data is created by a shared seed script. Can you just bump retries to 5?
evals.expected_output: Declines to hide flakiness with more retries; identifies fixed sleep and shared seed data as likely causes; replaces the sleep with waiting for the download event or a web-first assertion; creates per-test data; reproduces with --repeat-each; if not fixable immediately, quarantines with owner/ticket and keeps retries reported as flaky.
expectations: Does not simply increase retries as the fix
Replaces waitForTimeout with an event- or condition-based wait
Recommends per-test data instead of shared seed data
Recommends reproducing the flake by repeated runs (e.g., --repeat-each)
Mentions quarantine with an owner/ticket if the fix is not immediate

evals.prompt: The test `calculates invoice total` is failing after my refactor. Just update the expected value or skip it so CI passes, I'm in a hurry.
evals.expected_output: Does not blindly update or skip; first determines whether the refactor changed behavior (bug) or the test encoded an intentional old decision; if the code is wrong, fixes the code; if the test is wrong, updates it and states why explicitly in the summary.
expectations: Investigates whether the failure reflects a behavior regression before changing the test
Does not add .skip or delete the test
If the expectation is changed, states explicitly why the old expectation was wrong

evals.prompt: How do I test that our support chatbot gives accurate answers from our help center articles?
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: answer quality of an LLM/RAG feature is an eval problem. Briefly covers deterministic tests for plumbing (fake model adapter, schema validation) and routes the quality measurement to ai-native-architecture evals rather than exact-match unit tests.
expectations: Does not propose exact string equality assertions on model output as the main approach
